Section(s): 2.3. Extension to variable number of reduced and oxidized surface centers; Table 4

Text and equations in reading order:
    where $ \phi $ represents the total amount of reduced centers and $ 1 - \phi $ the total amount of oxidized centers. Following Ovesen et al. (1997), $ \phi $ can be calculated from the equilibrium relations as follows
(22) \phi=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{\gamma^{*}}{\gamma_{0}}\right)    [code: algebraic, computes \phi, code proposes definition]
    with
(23) \frac{\gamma^{*}}{\gamma_{0}}=\frac{1-\sqrt{K_{1}K_{2}\frac{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}p_{\mathrm{C O}}}{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}p_{\mathrm{C O}_{2}}}}}{1+\sqrt{K_{1}K_{2}\frac{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}p_{\mathrm{C O}}}{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}p_{\mathrm{C O}_{2}}}}}    [code: algebraic, computes ?, code proposes constitutive]
    The ratio in $ \frac{\gamma}{\gamma_{0}} $ is the relative free energy contact surface of Cu and Zn (see Fig. 1) (Ovesen et al., 1997; Vesborg et al., 2009). It can be related to the catalyst morphology using the Wulff construction framework (Clausen et al., 1994; Wulff, 1901). The equilibrium constants $ K_{1} $ and $ K_{2} $ (Eqs. (20) and (21)) can be expressed as a function of free energy according to
(24) K_{1}=\frac{k_{1}^{+}}{k_{1}^{-}}=\exp\left(\frac{-\Delta G_{1}}{RT}\right)    [code: algebraic, computes K_{1}, code proposes constitutive]

Symbols:
  \phi: fraction of reduced surface centers [-] (computed)
  \gamma^{*}: relative free energy contact surface of Cu and Zn (numerator in the gamma*/gamma0 ratio) [-] (computed)
  \gamma_{0}: reference free energy contact surface of Cu and Zn (denominator in the gamma*/gamma0 ratio) [-] (computed)
  K_{1}: equilibrium constant K1 [-] (computed)
  K_{2}: equilibrium constant K2 [-] (computed)
  p_{H_2}: partial pressure of hydrogen (variable)
  p_{CO}: partial pressure of CO (variable)
  p_{H_2O}: partial pressure of water vapor [bar] (variable)
  p_{CO_2}: partial pressure of CO2 in the gas phase (variable)
  k_{1}: forward rate constant for CO hydrogenation (parameter)
  \Delta G_{1}: standard Gibbs free energy change for reaction 1 [J mol^-1] (parameter)
  R: gas constant [J mol^-1 K^-1] (parameter)
  T: process temperature [K] (variable)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Catalyst deactivation neglected; only reactions (1)-(3) considered.
  - Langmuir‑Hinshelwood mechanism with adsorption, surface reaction, desorption.
  - Oxidized centers (⊙) are active for CO hydrogenation.
  - Reduced centers (∗) are active for CO₂ hydrogenation.
  - Total numbers of oxidized, reduced and hydrogen centers are constant.
  - Fast steps are at quasi‑equilibrium.
  - Quasi‑equilibrium assumption for fast adsorption/desorption steps.
  - Lumped kinetics for reactions (1)-(3).
  - Two alternatives for φ: quasistatic (Eq.22) or dynamic (Eq.28).
